script: The ship that secretly delivered the atomic bomb was sunk four days later, and the Navy did not even notice. On July 26, 1945, the USS Indianapolis dropped off the uranium for Hiroshima, a cargo so secret her own crew never knew what they carried. She had crossed the Pacific at record speed, alone, with two marines guarding a welded metal canister day and night. Four days later, a Japanese submarine sent her to the bottom in twelve minutes. Nearly nine hundred men went into the water, and for four days, nobody came looking. They faced thirst, madness, and the deadliest shark attack ever recorded. Survivors later said the worst part was the mornings, counting who had vanished during the night. When rescue finally stumbled onto them, only three hundred sixteen were alive. But the darkest part came after, the Navy buried the story on the day Japan surrendered, then blamed the captain for losing his ship. Charles McVay was convicted while the enemy commander who sank him testified in his defense. It took fifty five years, and a schoolboy's homework project, to clear the name of the captain who delivered the bomb.
